newsitem.title: USA: Millstone leaves NU with further losses.
newsitem.headline: Millstone leaves NU with further losses.

text.p: Northeast Utilities Tuesday reported a second quarter loss of $64.4 million, or $0.50 per share, citing ongoing outages at the Millstone nuclear power station for the company's weak performance.

All three units at Millstone Station in Waterford, Conn., have been shut down for more than 15 months and will not return to service until the Nuclear Regulatory Commission formally approves a restart, the utility noted.
Primarily as a result of the Millstone outages, non-fuel operation and maintenance costs rose to about $461 million in the latest quarter from about $390 million a year earlier.

Northerast Utilities pointed out the second quarter loss was worsened by a nearly $30 million net increase in the company's reserve to cover nuclear compliance costs that will actually be incurred in the second half of 1997 and the first half of 1998.

The company also said its fuel and purchased power costs were about $278 million in the quarter, up from $200 million in 1996's second quarter when these costs were reduced by a $32 million reserve established in the first quarter of 1996.
